title: Constraint Without Unique Confirmation: The Logical Limits of Inferring Quantum Ontology from No-Go Theorems
content: The 1935 argument of Einstein, Podolsky, and Rosen (EPR) challenged the completeness of the quantum-mechanical description of physical reality. In contemporary discussions, this challenge is often taken to have been decisively answered by Bell’s theorem and by the experimental violation of Bell inequalities. This article argues that such a conclusion involves an additional interpretive step not warranted by the logical structure of Bell-type results themselves. By formulating Bell-inequality violations as conditional exclusion results on classes of ontological models, and by distinguishing theoretical constraint from unique ontological confirmation, the analysis shows that Bell-type no-go theorems do not by themselves establish the ontological completeness of the quantum state. The same point is extended to the Pusey-Barrett-Rudolph theorem: although it further restricts admissible ψ-epistemic models under preparation independence, it does not uniquely fix quantum ontology. The combined lesson of these no-go results is therefore one of constrained but non-unique admissibility, rather than direct confirmation of wave-function completeness. From this perspective, the methodological core of Einstein’s incompleteness concern remains open—not as a defense of local hidden variables, but as a continuing question about the relation between empirical success, theoretical constraint, and ontological commitment in quantum foundations.
